question: What was the targeted growth rate of the Eleventh Five-year Plan (2007–2012)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**9%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eleventh Five-Year Plan of India (2007–2012) targeted a **GDP growth rate of 9%**.
 
• It focused on **inclusive growth**, aiming to reduce poverty and ensure that economic benefits reached all sections of society.
 
• The plan emphasized investments in agriculture, education, health, and infrastructure to boost growth and improve quality of life.
 
• Though the target was 9%, the actual growth rate achieved was approximately **7.9%**, falling short due to the global financial crisis of 2008.
 
• It was approved under the leadership of then Prime Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, with Montek Singh Ahluwalia as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• Five-Year Plans were introduced in India in 1951 based on the Soviet model to promote economic development through centralized planning.
 
• These plans were formulated by the **Planning Commission** (later replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015).
 
• The focus of each plan varied, addressing different sectors such as agriculture, industry, education, and health.
 
 
 
• **Inclusive Growth**
 
 
• Inclusive growth refers to economic growth that is distributed fairly across society and creates opportunities for all, especially the marginalized sections.
 
• The Eleventh Plan aimed to bridge disparities in income, education, gender, and regions.
 
 
 
• **Global Financial Crisis of 2008**
 
 
• The crisis began with the collapse of major financial institutions in the United States, causing a ripple effect worldwide.
 
• India's economy was impacted, leading to slower GDP growth during the later years of the Eleventh Plan.
 
 
 
• **Transition to NITI Aayog**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by **NITI Aayog** in 2015 to adopt a more decentralized and participatory approach to planning.
 
• NITI Aayog focuses on fostering cooperative federalism and preparing long-term strategies for India’s development.
